requirements.title: Standard input for the runner
requirements.rationale: An embedder's verifier and phase runner must feed a program its input without falling back to a hand-written exec.CommandContext runner that has no process-group kill.

criteria.condition: ExecOptions.Stdin is nil
criteria.action: give the child the null device as its standard input, as before this change
criteria.contract: A child that reads stdin sees end-of-file at once; Outcome and Output are unchanged from the pre-change behaviour

setup: a bash-family shell is available (the test is skipped otherwise)
ExecOptions.Stdin is nil
check.pseudocode:
for call in [RunArgv(ctx, ['sh','-c','cat; echo done'], {Timeout:5s}), Run(ctx, 'cat; echo done', {Timeout:5s})]:
  res, err = call
  assert err == nil and res.IOErr == nil
  assert res.Output == 'done\n' and res.Outcome == OutcomeOK and res.ExitCode == 0
  assert res.Duration < 1s

criteria.condition: ExecOptions.Stdin is a non-nil io.Reader
criteria.action: copy the reader into the child's standard input through a pipe the runner owns, and close the child's standard input when the reader returns io.EOF
criteria.contract: A child that copies stdin to stdout produces Output byte-identical to the reader's content; IOErr is nil

setup: input is 256 KiB of deterministic bytes including newlines and NUL bytes, larger than an OS pipe buffer
check.pseudocode:
input = deterministicBytes(256*1024)
res, err = RunArgv(ctx, ['cat'], {Stdin: bytes.NewReader(input), MaxBytes: 1<<20, Timeout: 10s})
assert err == nil and res.IOErr == nil
assert res.Output == string(input) and not res.Truncated and res.TotalBytes == len(input)
assert res.Outcome == OutcomeOK
repeat with Run(ctx, 'cat', ...)

criteria.condition: the child exits or closes its standard input before reading all of the reader's bytes
criteria.action: stop copying, treat the unread input as no error, and classify Outcome from the exit status
criteria.contract: Returned error is nil; IOErr is nil; Outcome is ok when the child exited 0

setup: Stdin is a 16 MiB reader for each call
check.pseudocode:
for argv in [['true'], ['head','-c','1'], ['sh','-c','exec 0<&-; echo closed']]:
  res, err = RunArgv(ctx, argv, {Stdin: zeroReader(16<<20), Timeout: 10s})
  assert err == nil and res.IOErr == nil
  assert res.Outcome == OutcomeOK and res.ExitCode == 0
  assert res.Duration < 5s

criteria.condition: the Stdin reader returns an error other than io.EOF
criteria.action: close the child's standard input and record the read error in ExecResult.IOErr whatever the child's exit status, classifying Outcome from the exit status
criteria.contract: Returned error is nil; errors.Is(res.IOErr, readerErr) is true for both a zero and a non-zero exit; Outcome is ok or exit from the wait status

setup: readerErr = errors.New("source failed")
a reader that yields "partial\n" and then returns readerErr
check.pseudocode:
for code, want in [(0, OutcomeOK), (3, OutcomeExit)]:
  res, err = RunArgv(ctx, ['sh','-c','cat; exit '+code], {Stdin: failingReader('partial\n', readerErr), Timeout: 5s})
  assert err == nil
  assert errors.Is(res.IOErr, readerErr)
  assert res.Outcome == want and res.ExitCode == code
  assert res.Output == 'partial\n'

criteria.condition: the child has exited and the post-exit drain has finished and the Stdin reader is still blocked in Read
criteria.action: return the ExecResult without waiting for the reader, and end the stdin copier goroutine when the reader's Read returns
criteria.contract: The call returns within DrainIdle plus scheduling slack of the child's exit; no copier goroutine remains after the blocked reader is unblocked

setup: pr, pw = io.Pipe(); pr is wrapped to record each Read call and its return
nothing is ever written to pw before the call returns
baseline = runtime.NumGoroutine() before the call
check.pseudocode:
pr, pw = io.Pipe(); r = recording(pr); base = NumGoroutine()
start = now(); res, err = RunArgv(ctx, ['true'], {Stdin: r, DrainIdle: 100ms, Timeout: 10s})
assert err == nil and res.Outcome == OutcomeOK and now()-start < 1.1s
pw.CloseWithError(errors.New('late'))
eventually(2s): NumGoroutine() <= base
n = r.reads; sleep(200ms); assert r.reads == n

requirements.title: Which end of the output is kept
requirements.rationale: A caller reading a test log or a report wants its beginning, while every existing caller relies on tail truncation as the zero value.

criteria.condition: ExecOptions.KeepHead is false (the zero value)
criteria.action: keep the last MaxBytes bytes of the output preceded by the tail-mode marker, exactly as before this change
criteria.contract: Output is byte-identical to the pre-change Output for the same command and MaxBytes

setup: s is a 100-byte string of distinct printable characters
check.pseudocode:
res, _ = RunArgv(ctx, ['printf','%s',s], {MaxBytes:10})
acc = NewAccumulator(10, TruncateTail); acc.Write(s)
assert res.Output == '[90 bytes elided of 100 total.]\n' + s[90:] == acc.String()
res2, _ = RunArgv(ctx, ['printf','%s',s], {MaxBytes:10, SpillDir: tmp})
assert res2.Output == '[90 bytes elided of 100 total. Full output: '+res2.SpillPath+']\n' + s[90:]
assert res.Truncated and res.TotalBytes == 100

criteria.condition: ExecOptions.KeepHead is true and the process writes more than the effective MaxBytes bytes
criteria.action: keep the first MaxBytes bytes of the output followed by the Accumulator's head-mode marker, which names the elided byte count, the total and the spill or log path when one exists
criteria.contract: Output == first MaxBytes bytes + "\n[E bytes elided of T total. Full output: P]" with P present only when a spill or log file exists; Truncated is true

setup: s is a 100-byte string of distinct printable characters
check.pseudocode:
res = RunArgv(ctx, ['printf','%s',s], {MaxBytes:10, KeepHead:true})
assert res.Output == s[:10] + '\n[90 bytes elided of 100 total.]'
res = RunArgv(..., {MaxBytes:10, KeepHead:true, SpillDir: tmp})
assert res.Output == s[:10] + '\n[90 bytes elided of 100 total. Full output: '+res.SpillPath+']'
res = RunArgv(..., {MaxBytes:10, KeepHead:true, LogPath: tmp+'/run.log'})
assert res.Output.endswith('Full output: '+abs(tmp+'/run.log')+']')
assert res.Truncated and res.TotalBytes == 100

criteria.action: treat MaxBytes <= 0 as DefaultByteLimit (50 KB) in both head and tail mode
criteria.contract: DefaultByteLimit bytes with MaxBytes 0 or -1: Truncated false, Output equals the input, TotalBytes == DefaultByteLimit; DefaultByteLimit+1 bytes: Truncated true, TotalBytes == DefaultByteLimit+1, the retained window is DefaultByteLimit bytes (the first in head mode, the last in tail mode), and the marker reads "[1 bytes elided of <DefaultByteLimit+1> total.]"; exactly 64 bytes with MaxBytes 64: Truncated false, Output equals the 64 bytes with no marker, TotalBytes == 64, in both modes

setup: Stdin readers supply the output to ['cat'] so the byte counts are exact
check.pseudocode:
for head in [false,true]:
  for mb in [0,-1]:
    r = RunArgv(ctx, ['cat'], {Stdin: bytesN(DefaultByteLimit), MaxBytes: mb, KeepHead: head})
    assert not r.Truncated and len(r.Output) == DefaultByteLimit
    r = RunArgv(ctx, ['cat'], {Stdin: bytesN(DefaultByteLimit+1), MaxBytes: mb, KeepHead: head})
    assert r.Truncated and r.TotalBytes == DefaultByteLimit+1 and '[1 bytes elided of' in r.Output
  r = RunArgv(ctx, ['cat'], {Stdin: bytesN(64), MaxBytes: 64, KeepHead: head})
  assert not r.Truncated and r.Output == bytesN(64) and r.TotalBytes == 64

criteria.action: for any output byte sequence and any MaxBytes, report the same TotalBytes (every byte the process wrote) and the same Truncated (TotalBytes exceeds the retained window) in head mode as in tail mode
criteria.contract: TotalBytes is equal across the two modes and equals len(sequence); Truncated is equal across the two modes and equals len(sequence) > MaxBytes; the retained window before or after the marker has length min(len(sequence), MaxBytes) in both modes

setup: a fixed-seed generator producing at least 40 cases
check.pseudocode:
for (seq, mb) in gen(seed, n=40):
  t = RunArgv(ctx, ['cat'], {Stdin: bytes.NewReader(seq), MaxBytes: mb})
  h = RunArgv(ctx, ['cat'], {Stdin: bytes.NewReader(seq), MaxBytes: mb, KeepHead: true})
  assert t.TotalBytes == h.TotalBytes == len(seq)
  assert t.Truncated == h.Truncated == (len(seq) > mb)

criteria.condition: the process writes exactly MaxBytes bytes
criteria.action: return the whole output with no marker in both modes
criteria.contract: Truncated is false; Output equals the bytes written; TotalBytes == MaxBytes

requirements.title: A caller-named log of the full output
requirements.rationale: An embedder needs the complete output in a file it chose, and needs to know before the run starts if it cannot have one.

criteria.condition: ExecOptions.LogPath is set
criteria.action: write the complete interleaved stdout and stderr to that file as it arrives, independent of truncation
criteria.contract: After the call the file's content is byte-identical to the full output, including when Output is truncated; TotalBytes equals the file size

setup: a temp directory
a command that writes about 200 KiB alternating stdout and stderr lines: for i in $(seq 1 4000); do echo out$i; echo err$i >&2; done
check.pseudocode:
want = join('out%d\nerr%d\n' for i in 1..4000)
for head in [false,true]:
  res, err = RunArgv(ctx, ['sh','-c',cmd], {LogPath: log[head], MaxBytes: 1024, KeepHead: head, Timeout: 30s})
  got = readFile(log[head])
  assert err == nil and got == want and len(got) == res.TotalBytes and res.Truncated

criteria.condition: ExecOptions.LogPath is a relative path
criteria.action: resolve it against ExecOptions.Dir, or against the process working directory when Dir is empty
criteria.contract: ExecResult.SpillPath is the absolute resolved path, and the file exists there

setup: two temp directories tmpA and tmpB
check.pseudocode:
r1 = RunArgv(ctx, ['true'], {Dir: tmpA, LogPath: 'logs/run.log'})
assert isAbs(r1.SpillPath) and r1.SpillPath == join(tmpA,'logs','run.log') and exists(r1.SpillPath)
t.Chdir(tmpB)
r2 = RunArgv(ctx, ['true'], {LogPath: 'run.log'})
assert evalSymlinks(r2.SpillPath) == evalSymlinks(join(tmpB,'run.log')) and exists(r2.SpillPath)

criteria.condition: ExecOptions.LogPath is set and the call is about to start the process
criteria.action: create missing parent directories with mode 0o700 and create or truncate the log file with mode 0o600 before starting the process
criteria.contract: On unix the created directories have permission bits 0o700 and the file 0o600; a pre-existing file's old content is gone

setup: a unix platform
a temp directory tmp
tmp/old.log already contains "OLD CONTENT\n"
check.pseudocode:
log = join(tmp,'a/b/c/run.log')
res = RunArgv(ctx, ['sh','-c','test -f "$1" && echo present','_',log], {LogPath: log})
assert res.Output == 'present\n'
for d in ['a','a/b','a/b/c']: assert stat(join(tmp,d)).Mode().Perm() == 0o700
assert stat(log).Mode().Perm() == 0o600
RunArgv(ctx, ['printf','new'], {LogPath: join(tmp,'old.log')})
assert readFile(join(tmp,'old.log')) == 'new'

criteria.condition: the LogPath file or its parent directory cannot be created or opened
criteria.action: return an error without starting the process
criteria.contract: Returns (ExecResult{}, non-nil error); a marker file the command would have created does not exist

setup: tmp/blocker is a regular file, so tmp/blocker/run.log cannot be created
marker = tmp/marker does not exist
on unix and not as root, tmp/ro is a directory with mode 0o500
check.pseudocode:
for call in calls:
  res, err = call
  assert reflect.DeepEqual(res, ExecResult{})
  assert err != nil and logPath in err.Error()
assert not exists(marker)

criteria.condition: ExecOptions.LogPath is set
criteria.action: use the log file in place of SpillDir for that call, creating no temporary spill file, and report the absolute log path in SpillPath, including when the command printed nothing, and in the truncation marker
criteria.contract: SpillDir contains no agentkit-exec-*.log file after the call; SpillPath == absolute LogPath for a command with empty output; a truncated Output's marker names the log path

setup: spill = tmp/spill and log = tmp/logs/run.log
check.pseudocode:
r1 = RunArgv(ctx, ['true'], {SpillDir: spill, LogPath: log})
assert r1.SpillPath == abs(log) and size(log) == 0
r2 = RunArgv(ctx, bigCmd, {SpillDir: spill, LogPath: log, MaxBytes: 100})
assert 'Full output: '+abs(log)+']' in r2.Output
assert glob(join(spill,'agentkit-exec-*.log')) == []

criteria.condition: writing to the log file or to a SpillDir spill file fails after the process has started
criteria.action: stop writing to that file, leave the process running to completion, keep accumulating Output, and record the write error in ExecResult.IOErr
criteria.contract: Returned error is nil; IOErr is non-nil; Outcome is classified from the exit status; Output holds the retained window

setup: writeErr is a sentinel error
a package-internal test seam replaces the log-file writer, and in a second case the spill-file writer, with one that fails with writeErr after its first Write and counts later Write calls
on Linux an extra real-file case uses LogPath /dev/full, whose writes fail with ENOSPC
check.pseudocode:
for target in ['log','spill']:
  w = failingAfterFirst(writeErr); installSeam(target, w)
  res, err = RunArgv(ctx, ['sh','-c','printf first; sleep 0.1; printf second; exit 3'], opts[target])
  assert err == nil and errors.Is(res.IOErr, writeErr)
  assert res.Outcome == OutcomeExit and res.ExitCode == 3 and res.Output == 'firstsecond'
  assert w.writesAfterFailure == 0

criteria.action: never delete a LogPath file, whatever the Outcome
criteria.contract: The log file exists after calls ending in ok, exit, signal, timeout and abort

setup: a unix shell
a distinct LogPath under a temp directory for each call
check.pseudocode:
for (argv, opts, ctx, want) in cases:
  res, err = RunArgv(ctx, argv, opts)
  assert err == nil and res.Outcome == want
  assert exists(opts.LogPath)
assert readFile(cases[0].LogPath) == 'ok\n'

requirements.title: The reduced environment by default
requirements.rationale: The runner's nil environment inherited every credential in the process, while tools.Options already defaults to ReducedEnv (REQ-SEC-08).

criteria.condition: ExecOptions.Env is nil
criteria.action: run the child with ReducedEnv(nil)
criteria.contract: A credential variable set in the test process (for example AGENTKIT_TEST_API_KEY) is absent from the child's environment; PATH and HOME are present verbatim

setup: t.Setenv("AGENTKIT_TEST_API_KEY", "sekrit")
t.Setenv("MY_SERVICE_TOKEN", "tok")
check.pseudocode:
t.Setenv('AGENTKIT_TEST_API_KEY','sekrit'); t.Setenv('MY_SERVICE_TOKEN','tok')
for res in [RunArgv(ctx, ['env'], {}), Run(ctx, 'env', {})]:
  lines = splitLines(res.Output)
  assert no line has prefix 'AGENTKIT_TEST_API_KEY=' or 'MY_SERVICE_TOKEN='
  assert 'PATH='+getenv('PATH') in lines and 'HOME='+getenv('HOME') in lines
assert set(splitLines(RunArgv(ctx,['env'],{}).Output)) == set(ReducedEnv(nil))

criteria.condition: ExecOptions.Env is non-nil, including an empty slice
criteria.action: pass it to the child verbatim, with no variable added or removed
criteria.contract: A child given Env {"FOO=1"} sees FOO=1 and no credential variable from the parent; os.Environ() passed as Env exposes the parent's credential variables

setup: t.Setenv("AGENTKIT_TEST_API_KEY", "sekrit")
t.Setenv("MY_SERVICE_TOKEN", "tok")
check.pseudocode:
assert RunArgv(ctx, ['env'], {Env: ['FOO=1']}).Output == 'FOO=1\n'
assert RunArgv(ctx, ['env'], {Env: []}).Output == ''
out = RunArgv(ctx, ['env'], {Env: os.Environ()}).Output
assert 'AGENTKIT_TEST_API_KEY=sekrit' in out and 'MY_SERVICE_TOKEN=tok' in out

criteria.action: resolve a bare program name through the PATH of the environment the child runs with, so a nil Env resolves the same binary as the process PATH because ReducedEnv keeps PATH verbatim
criteria.contract: the nil-Env call returns Output "A\n" and Outcome ok: ReducedEnv(nil) kept PATH verbatim and the lookup used it; the explicit-Env call returns Output "B\n": the lookup used the child's PATH, not the process PATH

setup: binA contains an executable script agentkit-probe-04 that prints "A"
binB contains an executable script agentkit-probe-04 that prints "B"
t.Setenv("PATH", binA + PathListSeparator + original PATH)
check.pseudocode:
t.Setenv('PATH', binA + sep + orig)
assert RunArgv(ctx, ['agentkit-probe-04'], {}).Output == 'A\n'
assert RunArgv(ctx, ['agentkit-probe-04'], {Env: ['PATH='+binB+sep+orig]}).Output == 'B\n'

requirements.title: The outcome and error contract
requirements.rationale: An embedder must tell a timeout from its own cancellation from a failed or successful exit without parsing text, and must never see an I/O failure reported as a clean exit 0.

criteria.action: for any call that starts a process, return a nil error and an ExecResult whose Outcome is exactly one of ok, exit, signal, timeout or abort, classified from the state at the moment the child exited
criteria.contract: the error is nil; Outcome is one of ok, exit, signal, timeout, abort; Outcome equals the scenario's class: exit 0 → ok, exit k>0 → exit, self-signal → signal, Timeout → timeout, cancel or caller deadline → abort, cancel during drain → the class at exit; ExitCode is 0 for ok, k for exit, and 128+signum for signal on unix

setup: a unix shell
a fixed-seed generator producing at least 30 scenarios

criteria.condition: the caller's ctx is cancelled while the child is running
criteria.action: kill the whole process tree, grandchildren included, and classify the call as abort
criteria.contract: Outcome == OutcomeAbort; Duration is measured to the child's exit; a grandchild that would create a marker file after the kill never creates it

setup: a unix shell
marker = tmp/grandchild-survived does not exist
check.pseudocode:
ctx, cancel = WithCancel(bg); after(150ms, cancel)
res, err = RunArgv(ctx, ['sh','-c','( sleep 1; touch '+marker+' ) & sleep 5'], {Dir: tmp})
assert err == nil and res.Outcome == OutcomeAbort
assert 150ms <= res.Duration < 1s
sleep(1.5s); assert not exists(marker)

criteria.condition: the deadline derived from ExecOptions.Timeout expires while the caller's ctx is not done
criteria.action: kill the whole process tree, grandchildren included, and classify the call as timeout
criteria.contract: Outcome == OutcomeTimeout; Duration >= Timeout and is measured to the child's exit; a grandchild that would create a marker file after the kill never creates it

setup: a unix shell
marker = tmp/grandchild-survived does not exist
the caller's ctx is context.Background()
check.pseudocode:
res, err = RunArgv(bg, ['sh','-c','( sleep 1; touch '+marker+' ) & sleep 5'], {Dir: tmp, Timeout: 200ms})
assert err == nil and res.Outcome == OutcomeTimeout
assert 200ms <= res.Duration < 1s
sleep(1.5s); assert not exists(marker)

criteria.condition: the caller's own ctx deadline, shorter than ExecOptions.Timeout, expires while the child is running
criteria.action: kill the whole process tree and classify the call as abort, not timeout
criteria.contract: Outcome == OutcomeAbort

setup: a unix shell
marker = tmp/grandchild-survived does not exist
check.pseudocode:
ctx, _ = WithTimeout(bg, 200ms)
res, err = RunArgv(ctx, cmd, {Dir: tmp, Timeout: 5s})
assert err == nil and res.Outcome == OutcomeAbort and res.Duration < 1s
sleep(1.5s); assert not exists(marker)

criteria.condition: the child exits on its own and the caller's ctx is cancelled later, during the post-exit drain
criteria.action: keep the outcome classified at the child's exit
criteria.contract: Outcome is ok or exit from the wait status, never abort

setup: a unix shell
DrainIdle and DrainCeiling are both 10s, so the drain is still running when the cancel arrives
check.pseudocode:
for E in [0,3]:
  ctx, cancel = WithCancel(bg); after(300ms, cancel)
  start = now(); res, err = RunArgv(ctx, ['sh','-c','( sleep 3 ) & echo started; exit '+E], {DrainIdle:10s, DrainCeiling:10s})
  assert err == nil and res.Outcome != OutcomeAbort
  assert (res.Outcome, res.ExitCode) == ((ok,0) if E==0 else (exit,3))
  assert 'started' in res.Output and now()-start < 2s

criteria.condition: the child exits before any deadline or cancellation
criteria.action: classify the outcome as signal, exit or ok from the wait status and report the exit status in ExitCode, using 128+signum for a signal-killed child on unix
criteria.contract: exit 0 → (ok, 0); exit 3 → (exit, 3); killed by SIGTERM on unix → (signal, 143)

setup: a unix shell
check.pseudocode:
for (cmd, want, code) in [('exit 0', ok, 0), ('exit 3', exit, 3), ('kill -TERM $$', signal, 143)]:
  res, err = RunArgv(ctx, ['sh','-c',cmd], {})
  assert err == nil and res.IOErr == nil
  assert res.Outcome == want and res.ExitCode == code

criteria.condition: the call cannot start a process because argv is empty, the program is not found, LogPath cannot be opened, or creating a pipe or forking fails
criteria.action: return an error and run nothing; no other condition returns a non-nil error
criteria.contract: Returns (ExecResult{}, non-nil error) for exactly these start failures

setup: tmp/missing does not exist
tmp/blocker is a regular file

criteria.condition: cmd.Wait returns an error that is neither an exit status nor a signal, such as exec.ErrWaitDelay
criteria.action: record that error in ExecResult.IOErr instead of discarding it, and classify Outcome from the exit status
criteria.contract: Returned error is nil; errors.Is(res.IOErr, waitErr) is true; IOErr is nil on every call where no stdin, log, spill or Wait I/O failure occurred

setup: a package-internal test seam wraps cmd.Wait so that, after the real child has exited 0, it returns exec.ErrWaitDelay
check.pseudocode:
installWaitSeam(func(cmd) error { cmd.Wait(); return exec.ErrWaitDelay })
res, err = RunArgv(ctx, ['sh','-c','exit 0'], {})
assert err == nil and errors.Is(res.IOErr, exec.ErrWaitDelay)
assert res.Outcome == OutcomeOK and res.ExitCode == 0
removeSeam()
for call in cleanCalls: res, _ = call; assert res.IOErr == nil

requirements.title: The built-in shell tools are unchanged
requirements.rationale: The runner's new options are for embedders; the model's execute, run_command and powershell tools must produce byte-identical results.

criteria.action: call tools.Run or tools.RunArgv with their explicit Options.Env, KeepHead false, MaxBytes DefaultByteLimit and Options.SpillDir, and with Stdin nil and LogPath empty
criteria.contract: the printed environment holds MARK04=1 and the given PATH, and no AGENTKIT_TEST_API_KEY; for execute only the shell's own PWD, SHLVL and _ are added; the large output's Text begins "[1000 bytes elided of <DefaultByteLimit+1000> total. Full output: " and ends with END plus no status line: tail mode at DefaultByteLimit; Metadata.SpillPath lies under tmp/spill and matches agentkit-exec-*.log; no file other than the spill file appears in the workspace or tmp/spill

setup: tools.Options with a temp workspace, SpillDir tmp/spill and Env {"PATH=" + os.Getenv("PATH"), "MARK04=1"}
AGENTKIT_TEST_API_KEY is set in the test process
check.pseudocode:
opts = Options{Workspace: ws, SpillDir: tmp+'/spill', Env: ['PATH='+getenv('PATH'), 'MARK04=1']}
for tool in [executeTool(opts), runCommandTool(opts)]:
  env = tool.Execute(ctx, envArgs).Text
  assert 'MARK04=1' in env and 'AGENTKIT_TEST_API_KEY' not in env
  r = tool.Execute(ctx, bigArgs)
  assert r.Text.startswith('[1000 bytes elided of '+str(DefaultByteLimit+1000)+' total. Full output: ')
  assert match(tmp+'/spill/agentkit-exec-*.log', r.Metadata.SpillPath)

criteria.condition: a model command run by execute, run_command or powershell reads standard input
criteria.action: give it the null device (REQ-TOOL-06)
criteria.contract: The command sees end-of-file at once and does not block

setup: tools.Options with a temp workspace
check.pseudocode:
r = executeTool(opts).Execute(ctx, {command:'cat; echo after', timeout_s:5})
assert r.OK and r.Text == 'after\n' and r.Metadata.Outcome == 'ok' and r.Metadata.DurationMS < 2000
repeat for run_command and powershell

criteria.action: produce ToolResult.Text, the status line, Data, Error and Metadata byte-identical to the pre-change values for every ExecResult with the same Output, Outcome, ExitCode, Truncated, TotalBytes, SpillPath and Duration
criteria.contract: execResultToTool(res, timeout) deep-equals preChangeExecResultToTool(res, timeout) in OK, Text, Data, Error and Detail; Metadata is equal by value, including the ExitCode pointee

setup: preChangeExecResultToTool is a verbatim copy of execResultToTool and execStatusLine as they were before this spec, frozen in the test file
check.pseudocode:
for (res, to) in gen(seed, n=500):
  got = execResultToTool(res, to); want = preChangeExecResultToTool(res, to)
  assert got.OK == want.OK and got.Text == want.Text and got.Error == want.Error
  assert deepEqual(got.Data, want.Data) and deepEqual(*got.Metadata, *want.Metadata)

criteria.condition: the ExecResult a shell tool receives has a non-nil IOErr
criteria.action: leave the IOErr out of the tool result
criteria.contract: Text, Data, Error and Metadata equal those of the same ExecResult with IOErr nil

setup: base results: ok with output, exit 2, and a truncated timeout with a SpillPath

criteria.action: pass the existing tests in tools/tools_test.go and tools/reqtool06_test.go with no edit to either file
criteria.contract: git diff --exit-code base -- tools/tools_test.go tools/reqtool06_test.go reports no change; go test ./tools passes, including TestGrandchildDoesNotSurviveTreeKill, TestExecuteDoesNotLeakAPIKeys, TestExecuteTruncatesFromTheTail, TestRunCommandCarriesTheSameEnvelopeAsExecute and TestRunArgvResolvesTheProgramWithTheChildsPATH

setup: the commit this spec's work starts from is recorded as base
check.pseudocode:
assert sh('git diff --exit-code '+base+' -- tools/tools_test.go tools/reqtool06_test.go').exit == 0
assert sh('go test ./tools').exit == 0

requirements.title: Tool metadata on the result message
requirements.rationale: An embedder reads exit code, outcome and truncation from the transcript record rather than parsing `[exit N]` out of model-facing text.

criteria.condition: a tool's Execute function returns a ToolResult whose Metadata is non-empty metadata
criteria.action: set core.ToolResultMessage.Metadata to a copy of that metadata owned by the message, with its own ExitCode pointer
